title: Quantum Codes From Classical Annealing
authors: Michael A. Perlin, Matthew Steinberg, Ben Criger
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an adaptive simulated annealing algorithm to search for moderately-sized quantum error-correcting codes with high encoding rates and large distances. Our search targets two classes of stabilizer codes: (1) CSS codes, and (2) a subclass of CSS codes that we call ``self-dual with equivalent logicals'' (SWEL) codes, the latter of which which admit transversal implementations of logical Hadamard and phase gates that can be leveraged to construct fault-tolerant gate sets. The search is guided by an energy function that acts as a surrogate for the logical error rate in a code-capacity noise model, combining code distance with a count of minimum-weight logical operators to resolve the discrete plateaux that impede na\"ive distance optimization. For block lengths of up to [MATH] physical qubits, our search finds state-of-the-art CSS and SWEL codes whose distances frequently meet or exceed the variants of the quantum Gilbert-Varshamov bound. In addition to providing favorable seed codes for fault-tolerant architectures based on code concatenation, the codes found in this work are promising candidates for high-rate code demonstrations on near-term quantum computing hardware.
tldr: This paper uses simulated annealing to search for quantum error-correcting codes with high rates and large distances, finding state-of-the-art CSS and SWEL codes.
motivation: Finding good quantum error-correcting codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but the search space is vast and traditional optimization methods struggle with discrete plateaux in distance.
method: An adaptive simulated annealing algorithm is introduced, guided by an energy function that combines code distance with a count of minimum-weight logical operators to resolve plateaux.
result: For block lengths up to a few hundred physical qubits, the search finds CSS and SWEL codes whose distances frequently meet or exceed variants of the quantum Gilbert-Varshamov bound.
conclusion: The discovered codes are promising for high-rate demonstrations on near-term hardware and as seed codes for concatenated fault-tolerant architectures.

title: Hybrid LLM-Guided Search For Quantum Reservoir Architecture Design
authors: Gautami Sanjay Naik Krishna Bhatia
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) uses fixed quantum dynamics as a high-dimensional temporal feature map and trains only a lightweight classical readout. QRC is attractive for near-term quantum machine learning, but its performance depends strongly on architecture choices such as input encoding, reservoir depth, entanglement topology, measurement features, state-reset policy, feature construction, and readout regularization. We introduce \method, a simulator-based benchmark that formulates QRC design as constrained black-box architecture search and evaluates whether large language models can act as proposal controllers for this search problem. The benchmark compares five policies under identical evaluation budgets: random search, evolutionary search, Bayesian/TPE optimization, a feedback-based LLM agent, and \hybrid, which combines LLM proposals with memory, mutation, crossover, duplicate avoidance, and exploration. On NARMA10, Mackey-Glass forecasting, and temporal parity, \hybrid{} is the most consistent policy: it ranks first on NARMA10 and temporal parity and second on Mackey-Glass, narrowly behind evolutionary search. Under a 25-evaluation budget and three seeds, \hybrid{} improves over random search on all tasks, including a 23.6\% relative reduction in Mackey-Glass error. The results do not show that LLMs are universal QRC optimizers; rather, they show that generative models can be useful high-level controllers when embedded inside validated, reproducible hybrid search loops.
tldr: This paper uses LLMs to guide the search for optimal quantum reservoir computing architectures, but the focus is on machine learning and optimization rather than core quantum information theory.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing performance depends on many architecture choices, and manual design is inefficient.
method: The authors propose a hybrid LLM-guided search that combines LLM proposals with evolutionary operators and memory, and benchmark it against random, evolutionary, and Bayesian optimization.
result: The hybrid method achieves the best or second-best performance on three temporal tasks under a limited evaluation budget.
conclusion: LLMs can serve as useful high-level controllers for architecture search when embedded in a hybrid loop, but are not universal optimizers.

title: A Reduction Scheme For General-order Ising-like Hamiltonians In Quantum Heuristic Solvers
authors: Chengsi Mao, Pavel Mosharev, Yao Wang, Man-Hong Yung
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Ising model is ubiquitous in various optimization problems but notoriously difficult to solve due to combinatorial explosion. In view of this, Hamiltonian reduction is a useful preprocessing technique for reducing the effective problem size before applying heuristic solvers. However, existing reduction techniques mainly target second-order Ising models, whereas many pseudo-Boolean formulations naturally contain higher-order interactions. In this work, we generalize the concept of non-separable groups to arbitrary-order Ising-like models and develop a Hamiltonian reduction framework that iteratively detects and merges constrained spin groups into single variables. We benchmark the reduction on synthetic hypergraphs and higher-order network datasets, and evaluate its integration with downstream order-reduction and solver workflows. Our results establish a foundation for Hamiltonian reduction in higher-order Ising-like optimization problems.
tldr: This paper proposes a Hamiltonian reduction framework for higher-order Ising-like models to reduce problem size before applying heuristic solvers.
motivation: Existing reduction techniques mainly target second-order Ising models, but many optimization problems naturally contain higher-order interactions, leading to combinatorial explosion.
method: The authors generalize non-separable groups to arbitrary-order Ising-like Hamiltonians and develop an iterative reduction framework that detects and merges constrained spin groups into single variables.
result: The reduction is benchmarked on synthetic hypergraphs and higher-order network datasets, showing effective problem size reduction when integrated with downstream solvers.
conclusion: The framework establishes a foundation for Hamiltonian reduction in higher-order Ising-like optimization problems, potentially improving solver efficiency.

title: The Quantum Adiabatic Theorem For Non-Hermitian Dynamics
authors: G. M. V. S. Aponso, B. P. W. Fernando, K. K. W. A. S. Kumara, R. P. K. de Silva
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a quantitative adiabatic estimate for a class of finite-dimensional non-Hermitian Schr\"odinger dynamics. The original non-Hermitian Hamiltonian is assumed to be diagonalizable with real spectrum and non-crossing eigenvalues. We then construct a dynamically compatible time-dependent metric operator, and its positive square root defines a Dyson map. The associated Dyson-transformed Hamiltonian is Hermitian. When this Dyson-transformed Hamiltonian satisfies the Hermitian adiabatic assumption, the standard resolvent-projection method gives an explicit adiabatic estimate in the Hermitian representation. Pulling this estimate back through the Dyson map gives an approximation in the original non-Hermitian representation. The resulting Dyson-pulled-back projections are then compared with the spectral projections of the original non-Hermitian Hamiltonian by using a contour-resolvent estimate. The final bound contains two contributions: the pulled-back Hermitian adiabatic error and the projection-comparison error. A two-level non-Hermitian model is presented to illustrate the hypotheses of the theorem and the two contributions appearing in the final estimate.
tldr: This paper proves a quantum adiabatic theorem for non-Hermitian dynamics with real spectra using a Dyson map to a Hermitian system.
motivation: Extend the quantum adiabatic theorem to non-Hermitian systems, which are relevant for open quantum systems and PT-symmetric quantum mechanics.
method: Construct a time-dependent metric operator and Dyson map to transform the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian into a Hermitian one, then apply standard Hermitian adiabatic estimates and pull back the result.
result: An explicit adiabatic error bound for non-Hermitian dynamics, consisting of a pulled-back Hermitian error and a projection-comparison error.
conclusion: The adiabatic approximation holds for non-Hermitian Hamiltonians with real spectra under appropriate conditions, with a quantitative error estimate.

title: Band Engineering Of Exciton Polaritons In Resonant Polaritonic Metasurfaces
authors: Polina Pantiukhina, Daria Smirnova, Kirill Koshelev
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Polaritonic metasurfaces provide a versatile platform for engineering hybrid light-matter states through the interplay of optical resonances and excitonic excitations. Yet, predictive models often remain phenomenological and rely on coupled-mode equations. Here, we develop an effective Hamiltonian framework for exciton polaritons in resonant polaritonic metasurfaces, derived from a semiclassical single-pole description of excitonic polarization and a Green's-function description of guided-mode resonances. The resulting non-Hermitian Hamiltonian rigorously incorporates resonant photonic harmonics, multiple excitonic degrees of freedom, and radiative losses. The model reveals selection rules governing photonic-excitonic coupling classified by orbital multipole index and polarization, and shows that the minimal number of excitonic degrees of freedom equals the number of relevant photonic modes. We apply the framework to a bulk van der Waals WS[MATH] metasurface patterned into a hexagonal lattice of triangular holes and uncover a new geometry-controlled topological transition driven by dipole-quadrupole band inversion, distinct from the conventional breathing-honeycomb-lattice transition. Full-wave simulations confirm the predicted topological phase diagram and the emergence of photonic and polaritonic edge states at a topological interface. Our results establish a theoretical multimode framework for geometry-controlled bandstructure engineering in polaritonic metasurfaces, with applications in topological, chiral, and quantum integrated photonics.
tldr: This paper develops an effective Hamiltonian framework for exciton polaritons in resonant polaritonic metasurfaces, revealing a topological transition driven by dipole-quadrupole band inversion.
motivation: Predictive models for polaritonic metasurfaces often rely on phenomenological coupled-mode equations; a more rigorous theoretical framework is needed to engineer hybrid light-matter states.
method: The authors derive a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian from a semiclassical single-pole description of excitonic polarization and a Green's-function description of guided-mode resonances, incorporating resonant photonic harmonics, multiple excitonic degrees of freedom, and radiative losses.
result: The model reveals selection rules for photonic-excitonic coupling and predicts a geometry-controlled topological transition via dipole-quadrupole band inversion, confirmed by full-wave simulations showing photonic and polaritonic edge states.
conclusion: This work establishes a theoretical multimode framework for bandstructure engineering in polaritonic metasurfaces, with potential applications in topological, chiral, and quantum integrated photonics.

title: Decoder Comparability Across Quantum Software Stacks: Repeated-Round Surface And Digitized-GKP Syndrome Replay
authors: Dennis Delali Kwesi Wayo, Chinonso Onah, Rodrigo Alves Dias, Leonardo Goliatt, Zaher Mundher Yaseen Sven Groppe
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a contract-preserving, family-aware comparison of decoder behavior across four syndrome-generation stacks (PennyLane, Qiskit, Cirq, and a LiDMaS+ reference) under a fixed replay interface. Request streams from repeated-round surface-code and digitized-GKP circuits are replayed through BP, MWPM, and UF with matched controls. The unified matrix spans 24 cells and achieves line-level integrity: [MATH] request lines, [MATH] response lines, response ratio [MATH] in every cell, zero parse failures, and zero decoder-name mismatches. Fifteen warning-no-syndrome events occur only in GKP-Cirq rows. Within-family ordering is stable in both families ([MATH]); source-averaged flip counts are 2.435, 4.768, and 5.870 for surface and 1.595, 2.908, and 3.681 for GKP. Relative to MWPM, BP reduces mean intervention volume by [MATH] in surface and [MATH] in GKP. Source-vs-reference effects are family dependent, with larger coherent shifts in GKP. Source-bootstrap ranks remain unchanged, and hidden-truth sidecars add an outer-code logical-parity error-rate check in which UF has the largest source-mean rate in both families. The comparison is stack-aware, contract-verified, and avoids raw cross-family threshold-equivalence claims.
tldr: This paper compares decoder behavior across different quantum software stacks for surface and GKP codes, focusing on syndrome replay and decoder performance metrics.
motivation: To evaluate and compare decoder implementations across multiple quantum software stacks to ensure consistency and identify stack-specific effects.
method: The authors replay syndrome data from repeated-round surface-code and digitized-GKP circuits through BP, MWPM, and UF decoders across four stacks (PennyLane, Qiskit, Cirq, LiDMaS+), using a unified matrix and contract verification.
result: The comparison reveals stable within-family ordering, family-dependent source-vs-reference effects, and that UF has the largest source-mean logical-parity error rate in both families.
conclusion: The study provides a stack-aware, contract-verified comparison of decoder behavior, but avoids raw cross-family threshold-equivalence claims.

title: Markov State Models Revisited: Principles And Algorithms For Unbiased Observables
authors: David Aristof, Robert J. Webber, Daniel M. Zuckerman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Markov state models (MSMs) have become ubiquitous tools for analyzing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations because of their simple, powerful premise: although complete MD sampling may be impossible, the MSM can "stitch together" transition probabilities derived from local sampling to provide a global picture of kinetics and mechanisms. In the standard MSM framework, the available MD data is organized into a single transition matrix, which is then used to estimate all observables at a lag time chosen so the coarse-grained dynamics are approximately Markovian. This approach leads to avoidable model bias and motivates long lag times that obscure short-timescale processes of interest. In contrast, this paper shows how to obtain unbiased coarse-grained observables at any fixed lag time and for any fixed coarse-graining in the limit of infinite, properly weighted data. The central idea is to replace the single-matrix framework with two transition matrices -- one representing equilibrium dynamics and another representing source-sink recycling dynamics -- and use the correct matrix or matrices to estimate the matched dynamical observables.
tldr: This paper presents a method to obtain unbiased coarse-grained observables from molecular dynamics simulations using two transition matrices instead of one.
motivation: Standard Markov state models introduce bias and require long lag times, obscuring short-timescale processes. The authors aim to eliminate this bias.
method: The authors replace the single transition matrix with two matrices: one for equilibrium dynamics and one for source-sink recycling dynamics, and use the appropriate matrix to estimate each observable.
result: In the limit of infinite, properly weighted data, the method yields unbiased coarse-grained observables at any fixed lag time and coarse-graining.
conclusion: The proposed two-matrix framework removes model bias inherent in standard MSMs, enabling accurate estimation of short-timescale dynamics.

title: Localization Transitions Of Diffusion Dynamics In Physical Networks
authors: Jun Yamamoto, Ivan Bonamassa, M\'arton P\'osfai
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Network diffusion underlies many transport phenomena, with Laplacian modes setting how information spreads and relaxes. In physical networks, however, connectivity alone is not enough: node volumes introduce local dwell times that regulate how flow is stored before being propagated. Here we show that physical heterogeneity reshapes topology-driven localization, with the degree-volume ratio emerging as the relevant disorder parameter. We solve an analytical model in which ratio detuning qualitatively reorganizes the Laplacian spectrum, and demonstrate in empirical networks how degree-volume correlations shift extremal eigenmodes away from the nodes selected by topology alone. Our results reveal a general feature-rich-driven mechanism for localization control, showing that physicality non-trivially reshapes the disorder landscape governing network dynamics.
tldr: This paper studies localization transitions in diffusion dynamics on physical networks, focusing on the interplay between node volumes and connectivity.
motivation: Understanding how physical heterogeneity (node volumes) affects diffusion and localization in networks, beyond purely topological models.
method: Analytical model solving Laplacian spectrum with degree-volume ratio as disorder parameter, validated on empirical networks.
result: Degree-volume correlations shift extremal eigenmodes away from topology-selected nodes, revealing a feature-rich mechanism for localization control.
conclusion: Physicality non-trivially reshapes disorder landscape in network dynamics, offering new control over localization.

title: Tensor Network Machine Learning For Wildfire Susceptibility Mapping: From Grokking Dynamics To Quantum Mixedness Of Class Representations
authors: Domenico Pomarico, Alessandra Costantino, Gabriel Ramirez Sanchez, Loredana Bellantuono, Davide D' Al\`o, Mario Elia, Alessandro Fania, Francesco Giordano, Niloofar Kheirkhahan, Raffaele Lafortezza, Ester Pantaleo, Sabina Tangaro, Roberto Bellotti, Alfonso Monaco, Nicola Amoroso
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A quantum-inspired tensor network framework for wildfire susceptibility classification in the Gargano region is introduced, leveraging AlphaEarth embeddings and Matrix Product State models. The approach combines scalable geospatial representations with an interpretable quantum mask, enabling both binary and multiclass classification of wildfire susceptibility. Beyond predictive performance, the study reveals a pronounced grokking transition in the binary case and provides a detailed analysis of inter-class confusion in the multiclass setting. By introducing level-resolved mixedness diagnostics based on reduced density matrices, we show that the MPS classifier naturally encodes a hierarchy of class distinguishability, with non-adjacent categories becoming more separable than neighboring ones. These results demonstrate that tensor network models not only achieve competitive classification accuracy but also offer a physically grounded framework to quantify and interpret class separability in complex environmental datasets.
tldr: This paper applies tensor network machine learning to wildfire susceptibility mapping, with no direct connection to quantum information theory, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to improve wildfire susceptibility classification using quantum-inspired tensor networks, but the application is purely environmental and lacks quantum information or thermodynamics content.
method: They use AlphaEarth embeddings and Matrix Product State models for binary and multiclass classification, and introduce level-resolved mixedness diagnostics based on reduced density matrices.
result: The model shows a grokking transition in binary classification and reveals a hierarchy of class distinguishability in multiclass settings.
conclusion: Tensor network models can achieve competitive accuracy and provide interpretable class separability, but the work is not relevant to the specified research directions.

title: Enantioselective Optical Trapping And Characterization Of All Dielectric Disorder-enabled Chiral Particles
authors: Guilherme T. Moura, Tanja Schoger, Kain\~a G. Diniz, Marcel A. B. Morte, Diney S. Ether Jr, Leonardo de S. Menezes, Yicui Kang, Emiliano Cort\'es, Cyriaque Genet, Nathan B. Viana, Felipe A. Pinheiro, Paulo A. Maia Neto
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We trap submicroscopic silica spheres coated with randomly distributed titanium dioxide nanoparticles in optical tweezers with Laguerre-Gaussian modes and observe orbital dynamics that differ from those of achiral silica spheres. We show that the disordered nanoparticle coating generates an effective chiral geometry, giving rise to enhanced enantioselective chiral optical forces and a measurable modification of the orbital period. A theoretical model based on the Mie-Debye formalism, including optical aberrations, not only quantitatively explains the experimental results but also allows to characterize the Pasteur parameter quantifying the chiroptical response of individual composite particles. These findings constitute direct experimental evidence of chiral optical forces exerted by structured light beams on individual chiral particles and identify disorder-enabled, all-dielectric particles as a versatile material platform to tailor chiral optical forces at the nanoscale.
tldr: This paper demonstrates enantioselective optical trapping of chiral particles using Laguerre-Gaussian beams, with a focus on optical forces and chiroptical response.
motivation: To provide direct experimental evidence of chiral optical forces on individual particles and to develop a versatile platform for nanoscale chiral manipulation.
method: Silica spheres coated with TiO2 nanoparticles are trapped in optical tweezers with Laguerre-Gaussian modes; orbital dynamics are observed and modeled using Mie-Debye formalism with optical aberrations.
result: The disordered coating creates effective chirality, leading to enhanced enantioselective forces and measurable changes in orbital period; the model quantifies the Pasteur parameter.
conclusion: Disorder-enabled all-dielectric particles are a promising platform for tailoring chiral optical forces at the nanoscale.

title: Quantum Gravity Simulation: Quantum Simulation With A Minimum Length Based On The Generalised Uncertainty Principle
authors: Jack Keable-Elliott, David J. Bacon, Andrew Burbanks, Jaewoo Joo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a recipe for simulating one-dimensional quantum systems for low and high energies with [MATH] qubits within the framework of first quantisation. Assuming a minimum grid spacing [MATH] in the finite-difference method, the generalised uncertainty principle (GUP) is derived analytically and shows distinct properties for low- and high-energy quantum systems. In the low-energy regime, the GUP approaches to the standard Heisenberg uncertainty principle (HUP) for [MATH]. However, for finite [MATH], the GUP mathematically provides three different regions dependent on the average momentum and suggests that a wavefunction can exhibit a single-point localisation at the finite momentum uncertainty due to lack of grid resolution. We then derive a new expression for the high-energy momentum and focus on two specific cases relevant to relativistic aspects. First, if the HUP is relaxed and the high-energy momentum is matched to the special-relativistic one, the resulting GUP predicts the existence of a minimum length with non-zero mass for high energy despite the continuous limit [MATH]. Second, enforcing consistency with the HUP allows the recovery of a canonical high-energy representation with no minimum length. But this requirement brings incompatibility with the special-relativistic momentum and suggests a modified energy-momentum equation. Therefore, we believe that the proposed momentum formulation provides a novel pathway to investigate quantum gravity phenomena for high energy using quantum simulation tools.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum simulation recipe for one-dimensional systems with a minimum length derived from the generalized uncertainty principle, aiming to simulate quantum gravity phenomena.
motivation: To explore quantum gravity effects using quantum simulation tools by incorporating a minimum length scale into the simulation framework.
method: The authors use a finite-difference method with a minimum grid spacing to derive the generalized uncertainty principle analytically, and then formulate a high-energy momentum expression for simulation.
result: The GUP shows three regions depending on average momentum, and for high energy, a minimum length can exist with non-zero mass, or consistency with HUP leads to a modified energy-momentum equation.
conclusion: The proposed momentum formulation provides a novel pathway to investigate quantum gravity phenomena using quantum simulation, but the connection to the user's research directions is weak.

title: On Solutions Of The Killingbeck Potential And Clarifying Comments On A Related Analytical Approach
authors: Fatma Zohra Khaled, Mustafa Moumni, Mokhtar Falek
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The work presents analytical solutions to the Schrodinger equation for the Killingbeck potential, a Hybrid model combining harmonic, linear and Coulomb terms, and which is also an approximate model of Yukawa-type potentials. The radial Schrodinger equation is solved by means of the series expansion method, thus yielding the exact expressions of both bound-states solutions and eigen-functions for the systems; these systems include quarkonium and confined hydrogen-like atoms in plasma environments. Furthermore, we offer a constructive commentary on the work of Obu et al. (East Eur. J. Phys. 3, 146-157, 2023), with the aim of clarifying a mathematical misstatement used in their analytical treatment of analogous systems.
tldr: This paper solves the Schrödinger equation for the Killingbeck potential using series expansion, providing analytical bound-state solutions and eigenfunctions for quarkonium and confined hydrogen-like atoms.
motivation: To obtain exact analytical solutions for the Killingbeck potential, which models quarkonium and atoms in plasma, and to correct a mathematical error in a previous work.
method: The radial Schrödinger equation is solved via series expansion method, yielding exact expressions for bound-state energies and wavefunctions.
result: Exact analytical solutions for the Killingbeck potential are derived, and a mathematical misstatement in Obu et al. (2023) is clarified.
conclusion: The work provides correct analytical solutions for a hybrid potential and highlights the importance of rigorous mathematical treatment in quantum mechanical problems.

title: Weakly Nonlinear Dynamics Of Unstable Modes In Jammed Amorphous Solids
authors: Kota Noto, Harukuni Ikeda, Kuniyasu Saitoh, Hisao Hayakawa
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the structural evolution in jammed amorphous solids by analyzing the eigenmodes of a generalized Hessian matrix that incorporates spatial modulation via wave numbers. Unlike the conventional Hessian, this generalized formulation captures linearly unstable modes through a Fourier-based extension of the Hessian matrix, enabling us to study responses beyond the mechanically stable regime. We demonstrate that the excitation of unstable eigenmodes leads to structural rearrangements independent of the initial perturbation by the simulation. Furthermore, we derive a weakly nonlinear amplitude equation to describe the growth and saturation of these unstable modes, analogous to the Landau equation. Our framework provides a pathway to understand instability-driven configuration changes in disordered solids.
tldr: This paper studies weakly nonlinear dynamics of unstable modes in jammed amorphous solids using a generalized Hessian matrix.
motivation: Understanding structural evolution in disordered solids beyond the mechanically stable regime is important for materials science.
method: The authors analyze eigenmodes of a generalized Hessian matrix with spatial modulation and derive a weakly nonlinear amplitude equation analogous to the Landau equation.
result: Excitation of unstable eigenmodes leads to structural rearrangements independent of initial perturbation, and the amplitude equation describes growth and saturation.
conclusion: The framework provides a pathway to understand instability-driven configuration changes in disordered solids.

title: Super-Resonance: Interference-Driven Suppression Of Radiative Decay Across Wave Physics
authors: Igor V. Minin, Oleg V. Minin, Ilia L. Rasskazov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Super-resonance has been coined independently for collective modes of acoustic cavity arrays (Tolstoy), extreme high-[MATH] states of dielectric resonators in photonics, and magnon-polaron bound states in magnonics, and is now applied interchangeably to physically distinct phenomena. We organise this review around the one usage admitting a precise, field-agnostic definition: a mode whose radiative linewidth is driven toward zero by destructive interference among its radiation channels, [MATH], while the bare single-channel coupling remains large. The canonical realisation is the Friedrich-Wintgen scenario of two modes sharing a continuum. The same non-Hermitian eigenvalue structure recurs in Tolstoy's acoustic arrays, photonic bound states in the continuum and quasi-BIC supercavity modes, anapoles, dark modes of coherent perfect absorbers, parity-time-symmetric devices near exceptional points, magnonic dark modes, and topological edge modes. We survey these realisations field by field and distil transferable design rules and figures of merit. We then disambiguate super-resonance from two families sharing the "super-" prefix: coherent enhancement, in which coupling to the continuum is collectively increased rather than suppressed (Dicke super-radiance, superscattering, whispering-gallery modes); and integer-commensurability locking (mean-motion, wave-particle, and Floquet resonances). Amplification, as in black-hole super-radiance, is likewise distinguished.
tldr: A review of super-resonance phenomena across wave physics, focusing on interference-driven suppression of radiative decay.
motivation: To disambiguate the term 'super-resonance' and unify diverse physical realizations under a common non-Hermitian eigenvalue framework.
method: Survey of acoustic, photonic, magnonic, and topological systems exhibiting Friedrich-Wintgen-type interference, with comparative analysis of design rules and figures of merit.
result: Identifies the Friedrich-Wintgen scenario as the canonical mechanism and distinguishes super-resonance from coherent enhancement and commensurability locking.
conclusion: Super-resonance is a universal wave phenomenon with transferable design principles across fields, but it is not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Propagation Dynamics Of High-gain Vortex Beams In Symmetry-broken Media Via Forward And Backward Three-wave Mixing
authors: Fan Meng, Hao Zhu, Xin-Yao Huang, Guo-Feng Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, vortex light, a distinctive form of structured light, has attracted considerable attention owing to its unique properties and the rich physical phenomena arising from its interaction with matter. In this paper, we investigate the propagation dynamics of vortex beams in a symmetry-broken three-level system based on forward and backward three-wave mixing (TWM) processes. We find that both processes enable the transfer of high-gain vortex light, with the associated topological charges obeying identical algebraic relations. The forward process exhibits periodic oscillatory transmission and modulates the transverse spatial profile of the generated signal vortex field, whereas the backward process features stable transmission and produces a signal field with higher gain and improved fidelity. Under the Autler-Townes splitting (ATS) regime, the probe field detuning in both schemes has a negligible influence on the gain. Optical depth influences only the rate at which the gain approaches its maximum, while the peak value remains unchanged. These results constitute a meaningful extension of the work reported in reference [40] and may provide a feasible approach for quantum communication, quantum computation, and the generation of high-gain, high-fidelity vortex light.
tldr: This paper studies the propagation dynamics of vortex beams in symmetry-broken media via three-wave mixing, focusing on gain and fidelity of vortex light transfer.
motivation: Vortex beams have unique properties useful for quantum communication and computation, but their propagation in nonlinear media is not fully understood.
method: The authors theoretically analyze forward and backward three-wave mixing processes in a symmetry-broken three-level system, deriving equations for the signal field and examining gain and spatial profile.
result: Both processes transfer topological charge with identical algebraic relations; forward process yields oscillatory transmission while backward process provides stable, higher gain and fidelity.
conclusion: The results extend previous work and suggest a feasible approach for generating high-gain, high-fidelity vortex light for quantum applications.

title: Dirac-vortex Modes Beyond The Continuum Limit
authors: Jiayu Fan, Jiusi Yu, Aoning Luo, Yiyi Yao, Shijie Kang, Xiexuan Zhang, Haitao Li, Biye Xie, Xiao-Dong Chen, Xiaoxiao Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dirac-vortex modes (DVMs) in Kekule-modulated lattices provide a topological route to wave confinement and are commonly described by the continuum Jackiw-Rossi model, in which the initial phase acts as a redundant gauge degree of freedom and does not affect observables of the mode. Here we show that this picture breaks down in discrete lattices when the complex mass texture that induces the DVMs no longer satisfies the slowly varying envelope approximation. In this regime, lattice discreteness turns the initial phase into a physically observable parameter that shifts the DVM center. By further introducing a sublattice-antisymmetric perturbation, we convert this phase-dependent center motion into a continuous spectral response of the DVM, enabling its frequency tuning across nearly the entire topological bandgap. Our simulation and experimental results agree well with a revised continuum model accounting for the mode-center motion. Within this perturbative framework, the model shows that the frequency shift exhibits a sinusoidal-like dependence on the initial phase. These findings reveal initial phase-sensitivity of the DVMs realized in lattices, an important and basic feature absent from the ideal continuum Jackiw-Rossi model, and demonstrate initial phase engineering as a potential pathway towards reconfigurable photonic devices.
tldr: This paper studies Dirac-vortex modes in discrete photonic lattices, revealing that the initial phase becomes observable and can tune the mode frequency.
motivation: The continuum Jackiw-Rossi model predicts that the initial phase is a redundant gauge degree of freedom, but this assumption breaks down in discrete lattices, motivating a study of phase effects.
method: The authors use simulation and experiments on Kekule-modulated photonic lattices, comparing with a revised continuum model that accounts for mode-center motion.
result: They find that lattice discreteness makes the initial phase physically observable, shifting the mode center, and that a sublattice-antisymmetric perturbation converts this motion into a continuous spectral response.
conclusion: The work demonstrates initial phase engineering as a pathway for reconfigurable photonic devices, highlighting a feature absent in the continuum model.

title: Motility Destabilizes An Absorbing-state Flock
authors: Narayan Dutt Sharma, Subroto Mukerjee, Chandan Dasgupta, Sriram Ramaswamy
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Activity, when it takes the form of motility, is generally seen to promote order in many-body systems. Here we present a one-dimensional lattice model that, in the non-motile limit, exhibits absorbing ferromagnetic states. When activity is introduced through biased motility, these absorbing state are destabilised and the system instead undergoes a transition from an ordered flock to a disordered state as the alignment strength is decreased. A finite-size scaling analysis of physical quantities reveals a continuous transition with critical exponents satisfying the hyperscaling relation in one dimension, providing quantitative evidence for the activity-induced disorder.
tldr: A one-dimensional lattice model shows that motility destabilizes absorbing ferromagnetic states, leading to a continuous order-disorder transition.
motivation: To understand how activity (motility) affects ordering in many-body systems, contrary to the common belief that activity promotes order.
method: A one-dimensional lattice model with biased motility and alignment interactions is studied via finite-size scaling analysis.
result: Motility destabilizes absorbing ferromagnetic states, causing a continuous transition from ordered flock to disordered state with critical exponents satisfying hyperscaling in 1D.
conclusion: Activity-induced disorder is demonstrated, providing quantitative evidence that motility can suppress order in certain systems.

title: Slack-Free Deep-Unfolded Combinatorial Optimization Solver For Inequality Constraints
authors: Ryo Hagiwara, Shunta Arai, Satoshi Takabe
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum annealing (QA) is used to solve combinatorial optimization problems (COPs). When COPs are implemented on quantum annealers, they are typically encoded as quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems, but constraint encodings often increase the number of qubits and the embedding overhead. This issue is particularly important for COPs with inequality constraints, where standard slack-variable formulations introduce additional binary variables. Unbalanced penalization (UP) avoids slack variables, but the original UP formulation requires tuning two penalty coefficients and contains a squared residual term that can increase the number of quadratic couplings. In this paper, we propose the unbalanced penalization Ohzeki method (UPOM), which combines UP with the Ohzeki method for inequality-constrained COPs. UPOM replaces the two static penalty coefficients of original UP with an auxiliary-variable update and removes the squared residual term from the Hamiltonian used for sampling. We further propose the deep-unfolded unbalanced penalization Ohzeki method (DU-UPOM), which learns the step-size schedule of the UPOM update from training instances. Numerical experiments on random knapsack problems show that UPOM improves over original UP and that DU-UPOM reaches optimal solutions in fewer iterations than fixed-step UPOM and other baseline. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces the tuning and embedding burdens of UP while making the Ohzeki method trainable for inequality constraints.
tldr: This paper proposes a slack-free method for solving inequality-constrained combinatorial optimization problems on quantum annealers by combining unbalanced penalization with the Ohzeki method and deep unfolding.
motivation: Standard QUBO encodings of inequality constraints introduce slack variables that increase qubit count and embedding overhead, while existing slack-free methods require manual tuning of penalty coefficients.
method: The authors propose UPOM, which replaces static penalty coefficients with an auxiliary-variable update and removes the squared residual term, and DU-UPOM, which learns the step-size schedule via deep unfolding.
result: Numerical experiments on random knapsack problems show that UPOM outperforms original UP, and DU-UPOM reaches optimal solutions in fewer iterations than fixed-step UPOM and baselines.
conclusion: The proposed framework reduces tuning and embedding burdens for inequality constraints in quantum annealing, making the Ohzeki method trainable for such problems.

title: On Unconventional Discretisations
authors: Basil Grammaticos, Thamizharasi Tamizhmani, Ralph Willox
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present various discretisation techniques that mark a departure from the classical algorithms of numerical analysis, in the aim of preserving the physical behaviour of the solutions to the differential systems we are discretising, even for discretisation steps that are not very small. These techniques are inspired by the principles laid down by Mickens and are close to those proposed by Hirota and Kahan. Detailed applications of these methods are presented for the logistic equation and for the Lotka-Volterra system. We discuss the importance of preserving positivity whenever the latter is an expected property of the solution and give a practical rule for achieving this. Possible problems arising from the discretisations we propose are also discussed. A section is devoted to discretisations of integrable systems aimed at preserving integrability. Finally we conclude this review with a discussion of the possible relevance of a discrete space-time.
tldr: This paper reviews unconventional discretization techniques for differential equations, focusing on preserving physical behavior and integrability, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To present discretization methods that preserve physical properties of differential equations even for large step sizes, departing from classical numerical analysis.
method: The paper reviews techniques inspired by Mickens, Hirota, and Kahan, applying them to the logistic equation and Lotka-Volterra system, and discusses positivity preservation and integrability.
result: The methods successfully preserve positivity and integrability in the examples, but the paper is a review without novel results.
conclusion: Unconventional discretizations can be useful for preserving physical behavior, but the relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is not established.

title: Mc-bridge: A Modular Receiver-Chain Simulation Framework For OECT-Based Molecular Communication
authors: Ozgur B. Akan Hongbin Ni
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Organic electrochemical transistor (OECT)-based molecular communication (MC) receivers connect transport and binding to device current, noise, calibration, and detection. We present MC-BRIDGE (Molecular Communication Bioelectronic Receiver-chain Integrated Design and Guided Evaluation), a modular framework linking release, extracellular diffusion, finite-area observation, stochastic binding, and OECT transduction to charge-domain detection. On an independent electrical time grid, it generates sequence-wide multichannel colored noise, performs control-channel referencing and charge integration, and supports molecule-shift-keying (MoSK), concentration-shift-keying (CSK), and Hybrid decisions. Through common module interfaces, it estimates symbol error rate (SER) and decoded-symbol mutual information and analyzes inter-symbol interference (ISI). At nominal separation, the passive finite-area observer retains 27.5 percent of the center-point decision-charge magnitude, while correlation between the selective and control channels determines whether control referencing helps. After adaptive search, held-out records with seeds disjoint from search and calibration test the selected and next-lower budgets, yielding a tested-grid upper bound on the minimum budget meeting the SER target. This passive-field test resets receptor occupancy, excludes ISI, and calibrates thresholds on separate records at each operating point. Retaining transport and receptor memory instead produces high SER. Thus, geometry, covariance, calibration, and memory can change receiver conclusions.
tldr: This paper presents a simulation framework for OECT-based molecular communication receivers, focusing on modeling transport, binding, and detection in biological environments.
motivation: Molecular communication is a bio-inspired paradigm, but this work is heavily focused on engineering aspects of OECT-based receivers rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The framework models release, diffusion, binding, and OECT transduction, generating colored noise and supporting various modulation schemes to estimate symbol error rate and mutual information.
result: At nominal separation, the passive observer retains 27.5% of center-point decision-charge magnitude; control referencing effectiveness depends on channel correlation; memory effects increase SER.
conclusion: Geometry, covariance, calibration, and memory significantly affect receiver performance, highlighting the need for careful modeling in molecular communication.

title: Equilibrium Causal Games: Separation, Identification, And The Identifiability Of Cyclic Latent States
authors: Neda Nazemi Faraz Dadgostari
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Power grids, markets, and interacting populations, settle into feedback driven equilibria observed through unknown sensors. Our Equilibrium Causal Game (ECG) joins a game to its cyclic causal model, hidden inputs, sensor map, and rules for interventions and equilibrium selection; interventions edit declared objects and recompute equilibrium. Under stated conditions, ECG-separation is sound but incomplete in our examples. Back-door/half-trek routes identify observed queries. Yet for an untouched rotationally symmetric Gaussian block, second moments determine only a source-frame rotation, across which distinct-variable effects generically change. Unknown sensing creates a separate ambiguity. In passive stable linear models without self-effects, unknown wiring and full-rank unknown sensing leave [MATH] completely unidentified for [MATH]. Under LiNG, non-Gaussianity removes the source rotation; mechanism interventions separate sensing from interactions. With unknown support, invariant sensing, aligned responses, and well-posed single-target interventions identify [MATH] up to declared equivalence. Of [MATH] targets, [MATH] suffice exactly when the sole untargeted node directly parents all others; otherwise [MATH] are needed. Acquisition probes are excluded; known wiring gives no universal count. With nonlinear sensing, isotropic Gaussian source blocks admit hidden twists within and across blocks in labelled environments preserving required radial laws. Conversely, under stated positivity, informative one-block changes, rank, and irreducibility conditions, the finest independent source-block representation is identified within the stated alternative class up to block permutation and blockwise coordinate changes, but not downstream mechanisms or the sensor/interaction split. Together, these results show which causal conclusions equilibrium data support and which require targeted experiments.
tldr: This paper introduces Equilibrium Causal Games (ECG) to model feedback-driven equilibria in systems like power grids and markets, focusing on causal identification from equilibrium data.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in systems that settle into equilibrium is challenging due to feedback loops and unknown sensors; the paper aims to provide a framework for identifying causal structures from such data.
method: The authors define ECG as a combination of a game with a cyclic causal model, hidden inputs, and sensor maps, and analyze conditions for separation and identification using back-door and half-trek criteria, as well as non-Gaussianity and intervention strategies.
result: They show that under certain conditions, ECG-separation is sound but incomplete; second moments determine only a source-frame rotation in symmetric Gaussian blocks, and unknown wiring and sensing leave parameters unidentified unless specific interventions or non-Gaussianity are used.
conclusion: The results delineate which causal conclusions can be drawn from equilibrium data and which require targeted experiments, highlighting fundamental identifiability limits.

title: Extinction Depth And Q-ary Error-Correcting Codes For The Limited Permutation Channel
authors: Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy Noam Ben Shimon (yohananov)
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the radius-one limited permutation channel, errors consist of disjoint adjacent transpositions. A correcting code must separate distinct codewords: their error balls may not contain a common received word. Hamming distance does not ensure this, because disjoint swaps can make words differing in many positions confusable. For block-concatenation codes, earlier work tested each possible collision only through the longer initial block. This sufficient condition is not necessary: we exhibit a valid ternary block set that it does not certify. We introduce extinction depth, which tracks unresolved first-block pairs through later block extensions, and prove that their extinction at one common finite horizon certifies correction at every length. The criterion gives explicit [MATH] and [MATH] block sets with rates above [MATH] and [MATH]. No block-set-independent depth bound exists: we give an exact linear family, verify a quadratic formula for every [MATH], and derive a polynomial-time finite-graph test. For growing alphabets, the normalized correction loss lies between [MATH] and [MATH], while explicit finite-length covers improve finite-alphabet upper bounds. We develop a parallel directed-extinction theory for detection, including an all-length block criterion, a set unresolved by the earlier test, and exact corridor depth [MATH]. Stable type lifting yields optimal first-order loss [MATH], and weak-zigzag codes improve the [MATH] lower bounds. Finally, window restriction, cancellation, and a bounded pending-input frontier extend the criterion and its finite-state verification to every fixed displacement radius [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies error-correcting codes for the limited permutation channel, focusing on extinction depth and block-concatenation codes.
motivation: The limited permutation channel models errors as adjacent transpositions, and existing Hamming distance-based criteria are insufficient for ensuring correctability.
method: The authors introduce the concept of extinction depth to track unresolved first-block pairs through block extensions, and develop finite-graph tests and parallel directed-extinction theory.
result: They provide explicit block sets with rates above certain thresholds, derive bounds on normalized correction loss, and extend the criterion to arbitrary displacement radii.
conclusion: The work advances coding theory for permutation channels but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimal Break-Resilient Codes
authors: Canran Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Break-resilient codes protect a word against an omniscient adversary who breaks it at arbitrary boundaries between adjacent symbols. For binary codewords of length~[MATH] subject to at most~[MATH] breaks, the best known explicit construction for this model has redundancy~[MATH], whereas the information-theoretic lower bound is~[MATH]. In this paper, we close this gap by presenting a break-resilient code with redundancy~[MATH] when~[MATH] for a fixed [MATH], matching the information-theoretic lower bound up to a constant factor. The key idea is to compute a short algebraic fingerprint of the message, which enables the decoder to reject incorrect assemblies of the received fragments.
tldr: This paper presents optimal break-resilient codes that protect binary words against an adversary who breaks them at arbitrary boundaries, achieving redundancy matching the information-theoretic lower bound.
motivation: Break-resilient codes are needed to protect data integrity when an adversary can break a codeword into fragments at unknown positions. The gap between known constructions and the lower bound needed to be closed.
method: The authors compute a short algebraic fingerprint of the message, enabling the decoder to reject incorrect assemblies of received fragments, and use this to construct codes with optimal redundancy.
result: The proposed code achieves redundancy O(k log n) when k = O(n^{1-ε}) for a fixed ε>0, matching the information-theoretic lower bound up to a constant factor.
conclusion: The work closes the gap between upper and lower bounds for break-resilient codes, providing an explicit construction that is optimal in redundancy.

title: Investigation Of Steep For Secure Communications Over Simo And Miso Channels Subject To Full-Duplex Jamming And Eavesdropping
authors: Yingbo Hua Md Saydur Rahman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Secure communications over SIMO and MISO channels between wireless nodes are commonly encountered in applications and widely considered in the literature. This paper investigates such a problem by considering a newly proposed scheme called secrecy-message transmission by echoing encrypted probes (STEEP). We focus on a type of heavily eavesdropped channels where an aggressive eavesdropper (Eve) has multiple antennas and is capable of jamming and eavesdropping in the full-duplex mode. Assuming optimal jamming and eavesdropping by Eve, we present the secrecy rates achievable by STEEP in two forms: using SIMO channel in phase 1 and using MISO channel in phase 2, and vice versa. With any given channel condition between every pair of nodes and any finite jamming power by Eve, the secrecy rate of STEEP in either form is shown to be positive subject to a positive power in phase 1 and a sufficiently large power in phase 2. The connections between STEEP in either form and the conventional SIMO and MISO schemes are provided, and their secrecy rates are compared comprehensively subject to random fading channels and finite transmit powers.
tldr: This paper proposes a secure communication scheme (STEEP) for SIMO/MISO channels under full-duplex jamming and eavesdropping, focusing on classical wireless security.
motivation: To achieve positive secrecy rates in heavily eavesdropped wireless channels where an adversary can jam and eavesdrop simultaneously.
method: The STEEP scheme uses encrypted probes in two phases (SIMO and MISO) and analyzes achievable secrecy rates under optimal jamming by Eve.
result: STEEP achieves positive secrecy rates for any finite jamming power given sufficient power in phase 2, and comparisons with conventional schemes are provided.
conclusion: STEEP is effective for secure communications in adversarial SIMO/MISO channels, but the work is purely classical and does not involve quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Optimization Of Mimo Steep For Secure Communications Over Mimome Channels
authors: Yingbo Hua Dinglin Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A transmission scheme for secure communications, called secret-message transmission by echoing encrypted probes (STEEP), can deliver a positive secrecy rate, even when eavesdropping channels are much stronger than that between users, subject to sufficient asymmetric power allocations from users. This paper considers an optimization problem for STEEP applied to MIMO (or MIMOME) channels between multi-antenna users and multi-antenna Eve. We reveal for the first time a significant increase of the achievable secrecy rate of MIMO STEEP using optimized precoders.
tldr: This paper optimizes precoders for a MIMO STEEP secure communication scheme over MIMOME channels to increase achievable secrecy rate.
motivation: Secure communication over MIMO channels is important, and STEEP can achieve positive secrecy rate even when eavesdropping channels are strong. Optimizing precoders can further improve performance.
method: The authors formulate an optimization problem for precoder design in MIMO STEEP and derive solutions to maximize achievable secrecy rate.
result: They reveal a significant increase in achievable secrecy rate using optimized precoders compared to non-optimized ones.
conclusion: Optimized precoders greatly enhance the secrecy performance of MIMO STEEP, making it more effective for secure communications.

title: Harnessing Heterogeneous Data For Conditional Optimization Via Optimal Transport
authors: Qinyu Wu Jonathan Yu-Meng Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conditional optimization tailors decisions to contextual or event information, but its practical use is often limited by the difficulty of learning the relevant conditional distribution from finite samples of a target joint distribution. This challenge is especially acute when target joint data are scarce or unavailable, or when few observations fall in the conditioning region of interest. Related joint data may be available from multiple sources, such as different stores, markets, populations, or operating environments, but these sources may be biased relative to the target distribution and cannot be pooled naively. We develop a distributionally robust framework based on optimal transport (OT) for harnessing such heterogeneous data in conditional optimization. The framework constructs ambiguity sets over joint distributions using OT distances to empirical source distributions and optimizes worst-case conditional performance over plausible target laws. We propose three OT ambiguity sets that capture different ways of using heterogeneous sources: enforcing simultaneous source consistency, aggregating source discrepancies through weights, and centering the ambiguity set at an OT barycenter. We derive tractable reformulations, establish feasibility conditions, discuss parameter choices, and characterize the relationships among the formulations, revealing trade-offs between robustness, information aggregation, and computational complexity. We demonstrate the value of the framework through a conditional assortment problem using demand and product-feature data from multiple stores.
tldr: This paper develops a distributionally robust framework using optimal transport for conditional optimization with heterogeneous data sources.
motivation: Conditional optimization often suffers from scarce target joint data; heterogeneous related sources exist but are biased and cannot be pooled naively.
method: The framework constructs ambiguity sets over joint distributions using OT distances to empirical source distributions and optimizes worst-case conditional performance.
result: Three OT ambiguity sets are proposed with tractable reformulations, feasibility conditions, and trade-offs between robustness, information aggregation, and complexity.
conclusion: The framework effectively harnesses heterogeneous data for conditional optimization, demonstrated on a conditional assortment problem.

title: The Missing Two-point Inequality In Weissler's Conjecture
authors: Paata Ivanisvili Yi C. Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weissler's conjectured characterization of complex hypercontractivity on the Hamming cube remained open in the ranges [MATH] and [MATH]. Ivanisvili--Nazarov established the diagonal cases. We prove the remaining strict off-diagonal cases through the corresponding two-point inequality. In fact, our argument proves the two-point inequality for every [MATH] and, by duality, for every [MATH].
tldr: This paper proves the remaining off-diagonal cases of Weissler's conjecture on complex hypercontractivity on the Hamming cube.
motivation: Weissler's conjecture on complex hypercontractivity had open ranges; the diagonal cases were known, but off-diagonal cases remained unproven.
method: The authors prove the two-point inequality for all parameters using duality arguments.
result: They establish the strict off-diagonal cases, completing the characterization of complex hypercontractivity on the Hamming cube.
conclusion: The conjecture is now fully resolved, providing a complete description of complex hypercontractivity on the Hamming cube.

title: Rational Spectra For Finite Hadamard Pairs And Bounded Spectral Sets On The Real Line
authors: Zi-Jian Song Xiao-Ye Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every finite spectral pair \((A,\Gamma)\) with \(A\subset\mathbb Z\), \(\Gamma\subset\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\), and \(0\in\Gamma\) has a rational spectrum, that is, \(\Gamma\subset\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\). Our argument relies on a modulus rigidity theorem for generalizedVandermonde systems satisfying inverse-orthogonality relations, constructed by hyperbolic positive-definite kernels. Combined with Galois conjugation and Kronecker's theorem, this rigidity forces the associated exponential nodes to be roots of unity. As an application, using the periodicity and fiberization of one-dimensional spectra, we show that every spectrum \(\Lambda\) of a bounded measurable spectral set \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R\) with \(|\Omega|=1\) and \(0\in\Lambda\) is contained in \(\mathbb Q\). This rational-spectrum result completes a chain of equivalences proven by Dutkay and Lai, which reduces the full one-dimensional Fuglede's conjecture to its finite cyclic analogues over \(_n\).
tldr: This paper proves that finite spectral pairs with integer first component have rational spectra, and applies this to show that spectra of bounded measurable spectral sets on the real line are rational, contributing to Fuglede's conjecture.
motivation: To resolve the one-dimensional Fuglede conjecture by establishing that spectral sets must have rational spectra, reducing the problem to finite cyclic groups.
method: Uses a modulus rigidity theorem for generalized Vandermonde systems with inverse-orthogonality relations, combined with Galois conjugation and Kronecker's theorem.
result: Every finite spectral pair (A,Γ) with A⊂ℤ, Γ⊂ℝ/ℤ, 0∈Γ has Γ⊂ℚ/ℤ; every spectrum Λ of a bounded measurable spectral set Ω⊂ℝ with |Ω|=1 and 0∈Λ is contained in ℚ.
conclusion: The rational spectrum result completes a chain of equivalences that reduces the full one-dimensional Fuglede conjecture to its finite cyclic analogues.

title: Duality And Reverse Self-Dual Constructions For Hyperderivative Reed-Solomon Codes
authors: Hongchang Li, Zhihao Zhu, Weijun Fang, Jun Zhang, Sihuang Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hyperderivative Reed-Solomon (HRS) codes form a class of maximum-distance-separable codes under the Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman metric and may be viewed as a derivative-evaluation extension of classical Reed-Solomon codes. For generalized Reed-Solomon codes, the Euclidean dual is again a generalized Reed-Solomon code. In this paper, we investigate the corresponding duality problem for HRS codes. Using a residue-theoretic argument, we derive an explicit component-wise representation for the Euclidean dual of an HRS code. The formula shows that, in general, the Euclidean dual is not an HRS code. Instead, it is blockwise upper-triangularly equivalent to a reverse-order HRS evaluation code, where the reversal occurs in the hyperderivative orders within each evaluation block. In particular, for full-domain HRS codes with low multiplicity, the triangular transformations reduce to diagonal scalings, and the Euclidean dual is obtained as the row reversal of an HRS code. Based on this reverse-order dual structure, we further study reverse self-dual HRS codes. We establish explicit criteria for reverse self-duality and construct several families from additive and multiplicative coset structures.
tldr: This paper studies duality and self-dual constructions for hyperderivative Reed-Solomon codes under the Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman metric.
motivation: To understand the dual structure of HRS codes, which are a generalization of Reed-Solomon codes, and to construct reverse self-dual HRS codes.
method: Uses a residue-theoretic argument to derive an explicit component-wise representation of the Euclidean dual of an HRS code, and then establishes criteria for reverse self-duality.
result: The Euclidean dual of an HRS code is blockwise upper-triangularly equivalent to a reverse-order HRS evaluation code; for full-domain low-multiplicity codes, the dual is a row reversal of an HRS code. Families of reverse self-dual HRS codes are constructed.
conclusion: The dual of an HRS code is not generally an HRS code but has a structured form, enabling the construction of reverse self-dual codes.

title: Spatial Semantic Communication: When Semantic Transmission Meets Index Modulation
authors: Xinghao Guo, Yin Xu, Dazhi He, Hanjiang Hong, Zhiyong Chen, Cixiao Zhang, Yiyan Wu, Wenjun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current digital semantic communication systems have primarily focused on maintaining compatibility with conventional constellation-based modulation. In contrast, index modulation (IM) represents a more spectrally and energy-efficient alternative by exploiting additional dimensions for information conveyance. Recognizing this potential, this paper bridges the gap between IM and semantic communications by proposing a novel spatial semantic communication (SSC) system leveraging cutting-edge fluid antenna-IM (FA-IM) technology. Compatible with existing joint source-channel coding (JSCC) architectures, the proposed SSC system employs the residual quantization (RQ) approach to discretize analog semantic features for subsequent digital IM transmission. Notably, the proposed SSC system synergizes RQ and IM via a semantic-aware stream splitting scheme, which ensures that critical semantic information undergoes less severe channel fading, thereby further optimizing semantic transmission performance. Simulation results validate that the proposed SSC system effectively integrates the high fidelity of RQ, the reliability of semantic-aware splitting, and the spatial efficiency of FA-IM, thereby providing a robust solution for future digital semantic transmission.
