title: When Shippers Become Algorithms: Candidate Exposure, Information Design, And The Concentration Of LLM-Mediated Freight Markets
authors: Takahiro Ezaki, Naoto Imura, Katsuhiro Nishinari
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shippers are beginning to delegate carrier selection to large language model (LLM) agents. We ask what such delegation does to a freight matching market, and which platform design choices contain it. We carried out agent-based simulations in which fifty shipper agents, built on commercial LLMs from OpenAI (GPT), Anthropic (Claude), and Google (Gemini), procure truckload capacity for thirty days. The market implements the rules of digital freight matching: each load is offered down the shipper's ranked list of carriers (waterfall tendering), carriers have daily capacity limits, spot prices respond to congestion, and carrier ratings accumulate with transactions. We found three risks and one remedy that works. Agents converged at once: for a fixed sampled carrier population, the same carrier was the modal first choice of every model on day one, attracting up to 76% of requests. Because each agent picks from its own randomly drawn list of displayed candidates, the platform controls how many options each shipper sees; concentration rose steeply once lists exceeded about ten carriers, with the onset differing across models. Which carriers ended up dominant varied widely from one sampled market to another, and displaying true quality instead of estimated ratings changed neither the level nor this variability (by design, quality affects only what agents see, never delivery outcomes). Against these risks, disclosing each carrier's remaining daily capacity cut concentration by a third and doubled shipper surplus, while vendor diversification, list-order randomization, and popularity display showed no clearly detectable effect. Platform information design, ahead of model choice or model regulation, is the lever that works.
tldr: This paper studies the impact of LLM agents on freight matching markets, focusing on carrier concentration and platform design.
motivation: Shippers are increasingly using LLM agents for carrier selection, which may lead to market concentration and inefficiencies.
method: Agent-based simulations with 50 shipper agents using commercial LLMs (GPT, Claude, Gemini) in a digital freight matching market with waterfall tendering, capacity limits, and spot pricing.
result: Agents converged on the same carrier, concentration rose with list size, and disclosing remaining capacity reduced concentration by a third and doubled shipper surplus.
conclusion: Platform information design is more effective than model choice or regulation in mitigating concentration risks.

title: Reliability-Aware Hard--Soft Physics-Informed Neural Networks For Robust Learning Of Challenging Partial Differential Equations
authors: Duc Tien Nguyen, Hang Tran, Trinh Minh Tuan, Nguyen Duc Manh, Dinh Gia Ninh
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) provide a mesh-free framework for solving partial differential equations, but their training is often affected by loss imbalance, optimization stiffness, and difficulty in capturing localized or multi-mode solution structures. Hard-soft PINNs (HSPINN) alleviate part of this difficulty by embedding Dirichlet or periodic constraints directly into the trial space, but the resulting fixed admissible representation can still be poorly conditioned for sharp or heterogeneous residual fields. This paper proposes a reliability-aware hard-soft PINN (RA-HSPINN) that preserves exact embedded constraints while introducing a bounded learnable reliability field to modulate the interior representation. The method combines this reliability-aware ansatz with inverse-EMA global loss balancing and lightweight regularization, while retaining the standard mean-square residual form. The reliability field is a numerical modulation variable, not a physical parameter or calibrated probability. RA-HSPINN is evaluated on nonlinear Burgers equations, periodic convection, a mixed-boundary Poisson problem, and a mixed first-order Poisson system. Compared with HSPINN, it reduces the relative error by [MATH] for sharp-gradient Burgers, [MATH] for Burgers data with noisy and incompatible initial conditions, [MATH] for smooth periodic convection, [MATH] for localized periodic convection, [MATH] for mixed-boundary Poisson, and [MATH] for a multi-mode mixed first-order Poisson system. The results show that reliability-aware modulation is most beneficial when hard-soft trial spaces are admissible but difficult to optimize, especially in localized, unreliable-data, and multi-mode PDE regimes.
tldr: This paper proposes a reliability-aware hard-soft physics-informed neural network (RA-HSPINN) for solving partial differential equations, which is a machine learning method unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) suffer from training difficulties such as loss imbalance and poor conditioning for sharp or heterogeneous solutions. The authors aim to improve robustness by introducing a learnable reliability field.
method: RA-HSPINN embeds Dirichlet or periodic constraints exactly into the trial space and adds a bounded learnable reliability field to modulate the interior representation, combined with inverse-EMA global loss balancing and regularization.
result: RA-HSPINN reduces relative error compared to HSPINN on several PDE benchmarks, including Burgers equations, periodic convection, and Poisson problems, with improvements ranging from 20% to 80%.
conclusion: The reliability-aware modulation is most beneficial when hard-soft trial spaces are admissible but difficult to optimize, especially in localized, noisy, or multi-mode PDE regimes.

title: A Proper Euler Magic Matrix Of Order $5$
authors: Scott Duke Kominers
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An Euler magic matrix is an integer matrix [MATH] with [MATH] whose squared entries sum to [MATH] along both main diagonals; it is proper if its squared entries are pairwise distinct. Euler constructed an order-[MATH] proper example, and M\"{u}ller settled orders [MATH] (none exist) and [MATH], leaving order [MATH] as the smallest open case. We construct such a matrix, by rotating one of M\"{u}ller's "near-misses" under a mirror-symmetric coordinate pair so that the two diagonal conditions collapse to a single rational equation; the same invariant suggests a uniform approach to the odd orders.
tldr: This paper constructs a proper Euler magic matrix of order 5, solving an open combinatorial problem.
motivation: The existence of proper Euler magic matrices of order 5 was the smallest open case after Müller settled orders 3 and 4.
method: The author rotates one of Müller's near-miss matrices under a mirror-symmetric coordinate pair, collapsing the two diagonal conditions into a single rational equation.
result: A proper Euler magic matrix of order 5 is constructed, and the invariant suggests a uniform approach for odd orders.
conclusion: The construction resolves the open case and provides insight into the structure of Euler magic matrices.

title: The Irrationality Of $e$ And $\pi$
authors: L. Lerner
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unlike an ordinary fraction with an infinite numerator and denominator, an infinite continued fraction must be irrational. Euler was the first to show that the base of the natural logarithm [MATH] is irrational, by numerically estimating its continued fraction, and showing the infinite sequence of convergents [MATH] so obtained converged to [MATH] using the Ricatti equation. Hermite showed that the recurrence relations for these convergents correspond to the recurrence relations between certain improper integrals, so proving the continued fraction tends to [MATH] in the limit of infinite [MATH]. Here we provide a motivation for the integrals involved and obtain closed form integral representations for [MATH] and [MATH] for all [MATH]. An interesting feature, is that the above results provide a short cut to the standard proof of the irrationality of [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves the irrationality of e and π using continued fractions and integral representations.
motivation: To provide a novel and simplified proof of the irrationality of e and π.
method: Uses infinite continued fractions and closed-form integral representations for the convergents.
result: Obtains integral representations for the convergents and demonstrates a shortcut to the standard irrationality proof.
conclusion: The approach offers a more intuitive derivation of the irrationality of e and π.

title: Theorems Related To Fermat's Sums Of Two Squares
authors: Marc Wolf Francois Wolf
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the factorization of sums of two squares X2 + Y2. We show the existence of linear and quadratic progressions on X that generate both factorizations and alternative decompositions into sums of two squares. We are therefore naturally interested in the number of decompositions into sums of two squares of an integer n and relate it to its number of divisors d(n). Finally, we present an algorithm to obtain these decompositions using the sieve introduced in (1).
tldr: This paper studies the factorization of sums of two squares and relates the number of decompositions to the divisor function, presenting an algorithm based on a sieve.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the structure of sums of two squares and their factorizations, linking them to divisor counts.
method: The paper uses number-theoretic reasoning to derive linear and quadratic progressions for X that generate factorizations, and employs a sieve algorithm to enumerate decompositions.
result: Existence of progressions for factorizations and a relation between the number of decompositions and the divisor function d(n) are established.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into the classical problem of representing integers as sums of two squares, with algorithmic implications.

title: Waves 2026 Book Of Abstracts
authors: Lise-Marie Imbert-Gerard, Chrysoula Tsogka, Daniel Appelo, Thomas Hagstrom, Yann-Meing Law, Serge Prudhomme, Behrooz Yousefzadeh
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: WAVES 2026, 17th International Conference on Mathematical and Numerical Aspects of Wave Propagation Concordia University (John Molson Building), Montreal, Canada, June 22-26, 2026 WAVES 2026 is the seventeenth meeting in a long-running biennial series that has, throughout its history, alternated between Europe and North America to advance the mathematical and numerical study of wave propagation. Hosted at the John Molson Building of Concordia University in Montreal from June 22 to 26, 2026, the conference continues this tradition as a leading international forum where theory, computation, and application meet. The scientific program spans the full breadth of mathematical and numerical techniques for wave phenomena, from the modeling and analysis of the governing partial differential equations to the design, analysis, and implementation of efficient computational methods. Representative themes include acoustic, electromagnetic, elastic, and seismic wave propagation; scattering and inverse problems; high-frequency and asymptotic methods; finite element, boundary integral, and time-domain discretizations; and absorbing boundary conditions and domain truncation, with applications reaching across the physical sciences and engineering.
tldr: This is a book of abstracts for a conference on mathematical and numerical aspects of wave propagation, with no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The conference covers wave propagation phenomena in acoustics, electromagnetics, elasticity, and seismology, focusing on mathematical modeling and numerical methods.
method: The book compiles abstracts of presentations on topics such as finite element methods, boundary integral equations, and high-frequency asymptotics.
result: No specific research results are presented; it is a collection of ongoing work in classical wave physics.
conclusion: The content is entirely outside the scope of the user's research interests in quantum information theory and related fields.

title: Robust Hierarchical Matrix Compression Of Acoustic Volume And Boundary Integral Operators
authors: Alberto Almuna-Morales, Danilo Aballay, Ignacio Labarca-Figueroa, Elwin van 't Wout
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discretizing integral formulations of the Helmholtz equation yields dense linear systems. Hence, simulating acoustic models at larger scales or higher frequencies is typically constrained by memory capacity. Fast algorithms, such as hierarchical matrix compression, reduce the memory footprint substantially while controlling the approximation error in matrix-vector multiplications. However, the commonly used Adaptive Cross Approximation suffers from early-convergence problems, where the iterative construction of low-rank decompositions stops before reaching the targeted error tolerance. This failure arises when the error estimator does not capture significant components of the matrix structure under partial pivoting. This manuscript proposes a new diagonal convergence criterion, additional matrix elements for the pivoting strategy, an extended admissibility condition, and a sustained convergence check to improve the robustness of hierarchical matrix compression. These modifications improve compression reliability without increasing memory. We tested our compression strategy on various discretized volume and boundary integral operators. The computational results show that our approach successfully compresses all benchmark matrices within predefined tolerances, thereby resolving the early-convergence issues encountered in standard algorithms. This robust matrix compression was achieved at the same memory footprint as alternative compression strategies. Furthermore, a complexity analysis shows log-linear memory scaling with mesh refinement at constant frequency. Finally, we successfully applied our robust matrix compression algorithm to a coupled system of volume and boundary integral operators that models transcranial ultrasound propagation. This confirms the feasibility of our robust algorithm to accelerate large-scale simulations with high-resolution meshes in a biomedical application.
tldr: This paper presents a robust hierarchical matrix compression method for acoustic integral operators, addressing early-convergence issues in adaptive cross approximation.
motivation: Simulating acoustic models at larger scales or higher frequencies is constrained by memory capacity due to dense linear systems from discretized integral formulations.
method: The authors propose a new diagonal convergence criterion, additional matrix elements for pivoting, an extended admissibility condition, and a sustained convergence check to improve robustness of hierarchical matrix compression.
result: The proposed compression strategy successfully compresses all benchmark matrices within predefined tolerances, resolving early-convergence issues, with log-linear memory scaling.
conclusion: The robust algorithm is feasible for accelerating large-scale simulations, demonstrated on a biomedical transcranial ultrasound model.

title: Bilinear Systems With Quadratic Outputs: $\mathcal{H}_2$ Analysis, Optimality Conditions For Model Reduction, And Algorithmic Solutions
authors: Heike Fa{\ss}bender (institute For Numerical Analysis, TU Braunschweig), Serkan Gugercin (department Of Mathematics And Division Of Computational Modeling And Data Analytics, Academy Of Data Science, Virginia Tech), Till Peters
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bilinear systems with quadratic outputs (BQO) have recently emerged as an important system class, arising naturally in applications where both the dynamics and the quantities of interest depend nonlinearly on the state. Despite the growing interest in this class of systems, a systematic [MATH] framework for BQO systems has been lacking. In this paper, we develop such a framework by establishing an [MATH] inner product and norm for BQO systems, deriving output bounds in terms of the [MATH] norm, and obtaining first-order optimality conditions for [MATH] optimal model reduction. Building on these theoretical foundations, we propose an algorithm that computes a reduced BQO system satisfying these optimality conditions, and thus generalizing existing [MATH] optimal methods for bilinear and linear quadratic output systems. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated on two numerical examples.
tldr: This paper develops an H2-norm framework for bilinear systems with quadratic outputs, focusing on model reduction and optimality conditions.
motivation: Bilinear systems with quadratic outputs (BQO) are important in applications where dynamics and outputs depend nonlinearly on the state, but a systematic H2 framework was lacking.
method: The authors define an H2 inner product and norm for BQO systems, derive output bounds, and obtain first-order optimality conditions for H2 optimal model reduction, then propose an algorithm to compute reduced systems satisfying these conditions.
result: The proposed framework generalizes existing H2 optimal methods for bilinear and linear quadratic output systems, and numerical examples demonstrate its effectiveness.
conclusion: The paper provides a theoretical and algorithmic foundation for H2 optimal model reduction of BQO systems.

title: FullPASS: Geometry Optimization For Full-Duplex Pinching-Antenna Systems
authors: Morteza Barzegar Astanjin, Seyed Mohammad Azimi-Abarghouyi, Thomas Eriksson, Mikko Valkama
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes FullPASS, an in-band full-duplex architecture for pinching-antenna systems (PASSs) based on two parallel waveguides. The FullPASS transceiver simultaneously communicates with a single full-duplex user terminal over the same time-frequency resource: the transmit waveguide delivers the downlink signal, while the receive waveguide collects the uplink signal. Candidate pinching elements are placed along both waveguides, and the FullPASS transceiver jointly selects the active transmit and receive elements. We derive a geometry-based channel model for the downlink, uplink, and transmit-to-receive self-interference paths, including free-space propagation, in-waveguide propagation phase and attenuation, and the attenuation caused by upstream activated elements along each waveguide. The joint activation problem is formulated as a binary optimization that maximizes the bidirectional sum spectral efficiency while keeping the self-interference leakage at the FullPASS receiver below a prescribed threshold. To solve the resulting nonconvex combinatorial problem, we develop a two-stage algorithm. The first stage uses phase-anchored second-order-cone relaxations and deterministic rounding to generate binary trial activation patterns under a simplified propagation model. The second stage applies alternating best-improvement local search with add, remove, and swap operations evaluated under the full propagation model. Simulations show that the proposed method achieves an average sum spectral efficiency within 0.95% of exhaustive search on both the 13-by-13 and 15-by-15 candidate grids. On the 15-by-15 grid, it reduces the average runtime by more than one order of magnitude relative to exhaustive search and remains applicable to substantially larger candidate sets.
tldr: This paper proposes a geometry optimization algorithm for full-duplex pinching-antenna systems to maximize spectral efficiency while suppressing self-interference.
motivation: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) are a novel wireless communication technology, and enabling full-duplex operation requires careful selection of active antenna elements to balance downlink/uplink performance and self-interference.
method: The joint activation problem is formulated as a binary optimization and solved via a two-stage algorithm: first using phase-anchored second-order-cone relaxations with deterministic rounding, then alternating best-improvement local search.
result: The proposed method achieves average sum spectral efficiency within 0.95% of exhaustive search on 13x13 and 15x15 grids, with over 10x runtime reduction.
conclusion: The algorithm efficiently solves the antenna selection problem for full-duplex pinching-antenna systems, enabling practical deployment.

title: Online Optimization Of Difference-of-Convex Compositions With Smooth Mappings
authors: Jingwei Ji, Jong-Shi Pang, Renyuan Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study online optimization for a broad class of structured non-convex non-smooth problems where each loss is a composition of a difference-of-convex function with a smooth mapping, and the feasible region is defined by constraint functions of the same kind. We propose a time-smoothed proximal linear algorithm and a local-regret measure based on a proximal residual mapping. We show that this residual is a proper stationarity measure for the original problem: its fixed-point condition implies first-order stationarity. Our analysis relies on a tangent-cone characterization for a feasible region described by composite difference-of-convex constraints, which is of independent interest and allows each update to be computed via a convex optimization oracle, despite the non-convexity of the problem. We establish a local-regret bound and a bound on the total number of inner convex subproblems. We also derive an error bound connecting the proximal residual to the distance to stationarity, providing a quantitative certificate of approximate stationarity.
tldr: This paper studies online optimization for difference-of-convex compositions with smooth mappings, a topic in non-convex optimization.
motivation: The authors aim to develop an online algorithm for a broad class of structured non-convex non-smooth problems that arise in machine learning and signal processing.
method: They propose a time-smoothed proximal linear algorithm and define a local-regret measure based on a proximal residual mapping, using a tangent-cone characterization for composite difference-of-convex constraints.
result: They establish a local-regret bound, a bound on the total number of inner convex subproblems, and an error bound connecting the proximal residual to the distance to stationarity.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm provides a practical method for online optimization of difference-of-convex compositions with theoretical guarantees on stationarity.

title: Optimization Models And Algorithms For The Unit Commitment Problem
authors: Javal Vyas, Carl Laird, Ignacio E. Grossmann, Ricardo M. Lima, Iiro Harjunkoski, Jan Poland
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The unit commitment problem determines the optimal strategy to meet the electricity demand at minimum cost by committing power generation units at each point of time. Solving the unit commitment problem gives rise to a challenging optimization problem due to its combinatorial complexity and potentially long solution time requirements. Our proposed solution approach utilizes a decomposition method in conjunction with alternative models from the EGRET library. Results of this decomposition approach tested against four benchmarking systems show that significant computational speed ups are achieved.
tldr: This paper addresses the unit commitment problem in power systems using optimization models and decomposition algorithms.
motivation: The unit commitment problem is critical for minimizing electricity generation costs but is computationally challenging due to combinatorial complexity.
method: The authors propose a decomposition method combined with alternative models from the EGRET library and test it on four benchmarking systems.
result: Significant computational speed-ups are achieved compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: The proposed decomposition approach effectively reduces solution time for the unit commitment problem.

title: Data-driven Feedback Rectification Of Switched Linear Systems
authors: Philipp Schmitz, Hannes Gernandt, Maria C. Honecker, Karl Worthmann
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, a data-driven method for the computation of stabilizing state-feedbacks is proposed that leads to a rectified eigenstructure of switched linear systems. This means that all switching subsystems have the same sets of eigenvectors and the rectification allows to compute a common quadratic Lyapunov function ensuring asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system. The method is illustrated for two examples including a model of an aerosonde.
tldr: A data-driven method for stabilizing switched linear systems by rectifying eigenstructure.
motivation: To compute stabilizing state-feedbacks for switched linear systems without a model.
method: Proposes a data-driven approach that computes feedback gains to align eigenvectors across subsystems, enabling a common quadratic Lyapunov function.
result: The method ensures asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system, demonstrated on two examples including an aerosonde model.
conclusion: Data-driven rectification is effective for stabilizing switched linear systems.

title: Beyond Ellipsoids: Semi-Algebraic Tightening For Chance Constraints Under Actuator Saturation
authors: Carlo Karam, Mirko Fiacchini, Matteo Tacchi-B\'enard
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by stochastic model predictive control applications, we present a semi-algebraic approach to constraint tightening for chance-constrained systems with unbounded additive disturbances and saturated inputs. The saturated error dynamics are handled via their exact piecewise-affine structure, which naturally accommodates asymmetric saturation bounds. A polynomial Lyapunov function satisfying a drift condition is then designed using sum-of-squares optimization, yielding finite-time probabilistic reachable sets and a probabilistic ultimate bound. The set geometry is explicitly optimized for constraint tightening, further reducing conservatism. A numerical example demonstrates the effectiveness of the design.
tldr: This paper presents a semi-algebraic approach to constraint tightening for chance-constrained systems with actuator saturation, using sum-of-squares optimization.
motivation: Stochastic model predictive control requires handling chance constraints with unbounded disturbances and saturated inputs, which is challenging due to nonlinearities.
method: The authors model saturated error dynamics as piecewise-affine systems and design a polynomial Lyapunov function via sum-of-squares optimization to obtain probabilistic reachable sets.
result: The method yields finite-time probabilistic reachable sets and a probabilistic ultimate bound, with explicit optimization of set geometry to reduce conservatism.
conclusion: The approach effectively tightens constraints for chance-constrained systems under actuator saturation, demonstrated by a numerical example.

title: On The Universality Of Simple Trust-Region Algorithms
authors: Clemens Sirotenko
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish universal complexity guarantees for quadratic trust-region methods and identify a common mechanism underlying their universal behavior under convexity, based on a function-gap model-decrease estimate that appears to be new in the trust-region literature. First, we prove that the basic trust-region method with inexact subproblem solves is universal under convexity. Under a [MATH]-H\"older-continuous Hessian, it attains the global complexity bound [MATH] for computing an [MATH]-approximate minimizer, without knowledge of [MATH] or the corresponding H\"older constant. In the nonconvex regime, the method retains the classical [MATH] first-order complexity bound under the usual additional bounded-Hessian assumption. With suitably vanishing inexactness, it also recovers Q-superlinear local convergence for [MATH] and convergence of order [MATH] for [MATH]. Second, we show that the same convex-universal mechanism applies to a trust-region variant with exact subproblem solves and a simple modification of the acceptance ratio. This variant is universal simultaneously in the nonconvex, convex, and local regimes: it attains the optimal nonconvex first-order complexity [MATH], while preserving the universal convex complexity and the local Newton rates. These guarantees require no knowledge of [MATH] or its H\"older constant. Both methods use the usual quadratic trust-region model and the classical radius-update mechanism, without gradient-dependent radii or model modifications such as cubic, gradient, or tensor regularization. The results show that the trust-region mechanism is inherently adaptive across nonconvex, convex, and locally strongly convex regimes, providing further theoretical support for the practical success of trust-region methods.
tldr: This paper proves universal complexity guarantees for quadratic trust-region optimization methods under convexity, nonconvexity, and local strong convexity.
motivation: Trust-region methods are widely used in optimization, but their universal behavior across different problem classes was not fully understood theoretically.
method: The authors introduce a function-gap model-decrease estimate and analyze two trust-region variants with inexact or exact subproblem solves, requiring no knowledge of problem parameters.
result: The basic trust-region method achieves optimal complexity bounds for convex and nonconvex problems, and a simple variant attains simultaneous universality across all regimes.
conclusion: The trust-region mechanism is inherently adaptive, providing theoretical support for its practical success.

title: Estimating The H\"usler--Reiss Variogram Matrix By Clipped Moments
authors: Johan Segers Shuang Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In multivariate extreme value analysis, the tail dependence between some of the risk variables at hand may be weak, even when other variables do tend to become large simultaneously. Weak tail dependence may induce a substantial bias in estimation procedures based on the limiting multivariate (generalized) Pareto distribution of excesses over high thresholds. We consider a H\"usler--Reiss multivariate generalized Pareto model and, motivated by this issue, propose first- and second-order moment estimators of its variogram matrix constructed from a lower-tail-clipped version of the underlying random vector. The asymptotic normality of the proposed estimators is established. We demonstrate by simulation studies that they have lower bias than the empirical variogram estimator in certain cases, particularly when the dependence between components is weak. The estimators are applied to flood discharge data from the Danube river basin and the US flight delay data, showing that the tail dependence structure implied by the fitted model based on the first-order clipped moment estimator aligns more closely with the empirical tail dependence of the data than that based on the empirical variogram estimator.
tldr: This paper proposes clipped moment estimators for the variogram matrix in a Hüsler–Reiss multivariate generalized Pareto model to reduce bias in weak tail dependence settings.
motivation: Weak tail dependence can cause substantial bias in standard estimation procedures for multivariate extreme value models, motivating the need for more robust estimators.
method: First- and second-order moment estimators are constructed from a lower-tail-clipped version of the random vector, and their asymptotic normality is established.
result: Simulation studies show the proposed estimators have lower bias than the empirical variogram estimator, especially when dependence between components is weak.
conclusion: The clipped moment estimators provide a more reliable tail dependence structure, as demonstrated on flood discharge and flight delay data.

title: A Phase-field Neural Solver For Moving Contact Line Problems With Dynamic Boundary Conditions
authors: Ziyan Chen, Jinpeng Zhang, Pai Zhang, Li Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase-field models based on the Cahn--Hilliard equation coupled with dynamic boundary conditions provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for moving contact line (MCL) problems. Although physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) offer a mesh-free approach for solving partial differential equations, their direct application to MCL problems remains challenging due to long-time error accumulation, sharp interfacial profiles, localized contact line dynamics, and complex contact angle evolution. In this work, we propose MCL-PINNs, a specialized phase-field neural solver designed for MCL problems with dynamic boundary conditions. The method is built on a discrete-time formulation and incorporates several key techniques, including a multi-network time-marching scheme, a relaxed distribution constraint on the neural network outputs, variable scaling for sharply varying solution features, adaptive loss weighting, adaptive collocation sampling with interface extraction, and, when applicable, symmetry preservation through neural network inputs. These techniques improve the capability of the neural solver in resolving sharp interfacial profiles and contact line motion. The proposed method is validated through three numerical examples involving droplet coalescence, shear-induced droplet deformation, and dynamic wetting in a heterogeneous channel. The numerical results show that MCL-PINNs significantly improve prediction accuracy and robustness compared with standard PINNs formulations, enabling reliable resolution of complex interfacial evolution and moving contact line dynamics.
tldr: This paper presents a phase-field neural solver for moving contact line problems using physics-informed neural networks.
motivation: Direct application of PINNs to moving contact line problems is challenging due to long-time error accumulation and sharp interfacial profiles.
method: The proposed MCL-PINNs method uses a discrete-time formulation with multi-network time-marching, relaxed distribution constraint, variable scaling, adaptive loss weighting, and adaptive collocation sampling.
result: Numerical examples show that MCL-PINNs significantly improve prediction accuracy and robustness over standard PINNs for complex interfacial evolution.
conclusion: The method enables reliable resolution of moving contact line dynamics in phase-field models.

title: On Odd Perfect Numbers With Exactly One Even Exponent Greater Than 2

tldr: This paper proves a divisibility condition for odd perfect numbers with a specific exponent structure.
motivation: Odd perfect numbers are a classic unsolved problem in number theory; the paper aims to narrow down possible forms.
method: The authors use elementary number theory and algebraic manipulations to derive the condition.
result: If all even exponents of an odd perfect number are 2 except one, then a specific factor divides the number.
conclusion: The result contributes to the characterization of odd perfect numbers but does not resolve the existence question.

title: A Structure-Adaptive Random Feature Method For High-Dimensional Elliptic PDEs
authors: Jiale Linghu, Hao Dong, Yangshuai Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Random-feature methods reduce high-dimensional elliptic PDE collocation to linear coefficient problems, but full-dimensional trial spaces overlook lower-dimensional structure. We introduce the Hierarchical Analysis-of-Variance Random Feature Method (HA-RFM), which selects coordinate blocks using closed Sobol indices of the PDE residual, identifies oblique low-rank features from fitted-predictor gradients, and couples all retained features in one regularized least-squares solve. Under structural and stability hypotheses, we establish an [MATH] error bound that links solution and residual truncation to finite-width approximation and regularized finite-sample fitting, and we derive guarantees for width and structure recovery. The resulting width is polynomial in the dimension at fixed interaction order, with dimension-independent higher-order contributions under uniform structural control. Residual screening achieves exact recovery of the prescribed three-pair support, while fitted-predictor gradients recover oblique directions through dimension [MATH]. In random-ridge tests, less than [MATH] additional width reduces errors by factors of [MATH]-[MATH] over coordinate blocks and [MATH]-[MATH] over equal-width full-dimensional RFM. Semilinear computations extend HA-RFM through dimension [MATH], while dense and distributed interactions delineate the coordinate families required for broader structure.

motivation: The paper aims to improve the efficiency of random feature methods for high-dimensional PDEs by exploiting lower-dimensional structure.
method: It introduces the Hierarchical Analysis-of-Variance Random Feature Method (HA-RFM) that selects coordinate blocks using Sobol indices and identifies oblique low-rank features from gradients.
result: The method achieves polynomial width in dimension at fixed interaction order and demonstrates significant error reduction in random-ridge tests.

title: Beyond Recency And Magnitude: Learning-aware Uncertainty Estimation For Safety Stock Under Evolving Forecast-error Distributions
authors: Luis Fern\'andez-Palacios, Manuel Ceballos, Yolanda Mu\~noz-Oca\~na
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a non-parametric approach to refine forecast-error histories for safety stock estimation without relying on error magnitude or recency alone. Using forecast-error data from a fast-moving consumer goods environment, we show that one year of errors is insufficient to characterize service-level risk, while pooling several years is problematic because error distributions change over time. Non-parametric annual comparisons indicate a progressive reduction in bias and dispersion, consistent with learning in the forecasting process. We propose LOWDII (Leave-One-Out Wasserstein Distributional Influence Index), a diagnostic that evaluates the distributional influence of each historical forecast error on the empirical uncertainty distribution used for safety stock calibration. LOWDII identifies observations whose influence is disproportionate to their representativeness, separating transient distortions from persistent tail behaviour without imposing parametric assumptions. We evaluate the method in a discrete-event simulation using subsequent-year demand realizations as validation. The results show that LOWDII achieves the target service level while reducing average stock by 5.1% to 22.6% relative to benchmark methods. From a managerial perspective, LOWDII helps firms translate improvements in the forecasting process into safety stock decisions, avoiding the projection of obsolete historical errors into the future and capturing the economic benefit of lower uncertainty requirements earlier.
tldr: This paper proposes a non-parametric method for safety stock estimation using forecast-error data, focusing on supply chain management.
motivation: Traditional safety stock methods rely on recency or magnitude of forecast errors, but evolving error distributions make historical data unreliable.
method: The authors develop LOWDII, a diagnostic that evaluates the distributional influence of each historical forecast error on the empirical uncertainty distribution, using Wasserstein distance.
result: In simulations, LOWDII achieves target service levels while reducing average stock by 5.1% to 22.6% compared to benchmarks.
conclusion: LOWDII helps firms translate forecasting improvements into safety stock decisions, avoiding obsolete historical errors.

title: Finite-horizon Quantile Martingale Posteriors: Raw-urn Laws And Matrix-gain Regression
authors: Nam Anh Le
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Martingale posteriors quantify uncertainty by forward-imputing observations from one-step-ahead predictive distributions, but implementations stop after finitely many imputations. For the empirical P\'olya-urn posterior of a quantile the law of the stopped state is derived. The quantile of the stopped urn measure keeps the familiar martingale tail-sum variance fraction; the deployed stochastic-approximation tracker with frozen gain [MATH] does not. Its variance carries an explicit factor [MATH] with [MATH], which may fall below or exceed the tail fraction, and a density-adapted gain restores calibration through a density-free inflation. Shared urn innovations yield the joint law of finitely many quantile levels. For conditional quantile regression, a smoothed martingale posterior started at the ordinary quantile-regression estimator with a full inverse-Jacobian matrix gain satisfies a process Bernstein--von Mises theorem with calibrated finite-horizon bands; scalar or diagonal gains cannot match the sandwich covariance process.
tldr: This paper develops finite-horizon quantile martingale posteriors for uncertainty quantification, focusing on Polya-urn and matrix-gain regression.
motivation: To provide calibrated finite-horizon uncertainty quantification for quantile estimation and conditional quantile regression.
method: Derives the law of stopped urn measures for quantiles, analyzes stochastic approximation trackers with frozen gain, and proposes a smoothed martingale posterior with full inverse-Jacobian matrix gain.
result: The quantile of the stopped urn measure retains the martingale tail-sum variance fraction, while the frozen-gain tracker does not; a density-adapted gain restores calibration. The matrix-gain posterior satisfies a process Bernstein–von Mises theorem with calibrated bands.
conclusion: The proposed methods yield calibrated finite-horizon uncertainty quantification for quantiles, with matrix gains outperforming scalar or diagonal gains.

title: Multi-domain Fem-bem Coupling With Several Impenetrable Obstacles
authors: Antonin Boisneault, Marcella Bonazzoli, Xavier Claeys, Pierre Marchand
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a recent paper we have analyzed a new formulation of the coupling of finite and boundary element methods (FEM-BEM) for Helmholtz problems, involving several heterogeneous bounded subdomains and one homogeneous unbounded subdomain. This formulation, called Generalized Optimized Schwarz Method (GOSM), is substructured, that is, its unknowns are associated with the subdomains interfaces. To derive the GOSM, the first step was to prove that a solution to the Helmholtz problem satisfies a specific multi-domain variational formulation, which involves one operator for each subdomain, each operator being independent of the others. In the present contribution, we design a variational formulation of that type for a more general geometrical and material configuration: several heterogeneous bounded subdomains, impenetrable obstacles and homogeneous subdomains are allowed. Note that, like in our recent paper, we assume that only one subdomain is unbounded, and that its boundary is bounded. The domain partition can have cross-points, that is, points where at least three subdomains are adjacent. We also prove that a solution to the initial Helmholtz problem can be recovered from a solution to the multi-domain variational formulation. This shows that the GOSM is a general and flexible framework to model acoustic wave propagation, as it can handle both multi-domain FEM-BEM coupling and (weakly imposed) boundary conditions on several obstacles.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for coupling finite and boundary element methods for Helmholtz problems with multiple subdomains and impenetrable obstacles.
motivation: To extend a previously developed multi-domain FEM-BEM coupling formulation (GOSM) to handle more general geometries including impenetrable obstacles and cross-points.
method: A variational formulation is designed that involves independent operators for each subdomain, and it is shown that a solution to the original Helmholtz problem can be recovered from the multi-domain formulation.
result: The GOSM framework is proven to be general and flexible for modeling acoustic wave propagation with multi-domain FEM-BEM coupling and weakly imposed boundary conditions on obstacles.
conclusion: The proposed formulation successfully handles heterogeneous bounded subdomains, impenetrable obstacles, and cross-points, demonstrating the versatility of the GOSM approach.

title: A Hierarchical Sparse-grid Particle Method For The Vlasov--Poisson System
authors: Fabrice Deluzet, Cl\'ement Guillet, Jacek Narski
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a hierarchical sparse-grid (HSG) particle method for the numerical solution of the Vlasov--Poisson system. Sparse-grid PIC methods have so far been formulated within finite-difference frameworks, most notably through the sparse-grid combination technique (SGCT), which ties them to tensor-product Cartesian grids and globally defined component grids. This paper brings sparse-grid particle methods into the Galerkin setting: the field equation is solved in variational form on a hierarchical sparse-grid space spanned by B-splines of arbitrary degree, and the traditional charge deposition step is replaced by a direct Galerkin projection of the raw Monte Carlo density estimator onto this space. Beyond preserving the mesh-complexity and noise-reduction benefits of sparse grids, this reformulation substantially extends the versatility of the approach, opening the way to spatial adaptivity and to non-rectangular geometries, which are notoriously difficult to accommodate within the SGCT framework. We carry out a probabilistic error analysis decomposing the numerical error into a grid-based bias and a statistical noise component. Under mixed-derivative regularity assumptions on the particle distribution, the bias of the charge density in the [MATH]-norm is shown to scale as [MATH], where [MATH] is the B-spline degree and [MATH] the spatial dimension, and the statistical error in the [MATH]-norm as [MATH], matching the accuracy of high-order SGCT-PIC methods. Corresponding bounds are derived for the electric field. The theoretical estimates are validated on classical kinetic plasma benchmarks, including configurations with limited regularity and strong anisotropies that are known to be challenging for sparse-PIC approximations.
tldr: This paper presents a hierarchical sparse-grid particle method for the Vlasov-Poisson system, a numerical method for plasma physics simulations.
motivation: Sparse-grid particle-in-cell methods have been limited to finite-difference frameworks with tensor-product grids; the authors aim to extend them to a Galerkin setting for greater flexibility.
method: The field equation is solved variationally on a hierarchical sparse-grid space using B-splines, and charge deposition is replaced by a direct Galerkin projection of the Monte Carlo density estimator.
result: The bias of the charge density scales as O(h^{p+1}) and statistical error as O(N^{-1/2}), matching high-order SGCT-PIC methods, validated on plasma benchmarks.
conclusion: The reformulation preserves sparse-grid benefits while enabling spatial adaptivity and non-rectangular geometries, advancing numerical methods for kinetic plasma simulations.

title: Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning For $N$-Player Stochastic Differential Games With Exploratory Policies
authors: Jing Zhang Jisheng Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study continuous-time reinforcement learning for [MATH]-player noncooperative stochastic differential games. Each player adopts an entropy-regularized exploratory policy; given the others' actions, the optimal response is a Gibbs distribution, and a Nash equilibrium requires these [MATH] conditional distributions to be jointly compatible. We prove that the natural equilibrium concept -- simultaneous Hamiltonian maximization -- is equivalent to this compatibility, and establish a necessary and sufficient condition expressed as a computable cross-partial criterion on the optimal [MATH]-functions. Nash equilibria exist unconditionally for decoupled and symmetric games. When compatibility fails, a coordinate path integral construction yields an approximate correlated equilibrium with explicit quadratic KL-divergence bounds that vanish locally uniformly as the exploration weight [MATH]. A [MATH]-function framework for the [MATH]-player game extends the single-agent [MATH]-learning theory of [21], with weak martingale characterizations motivating model-free on-policy and off-policy algorithms. The framework extends to the ergodic (infinite-horizon) setting with the same locally uniform [MATH] asymptotic rates.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time reinforcement learning for N-player stochastic differential games using entropy-regularized exploratory policies.
motivation: To develop a reinforcement learning framework for multi-agent stochastic differential games with exploratory policies and establish equilibrium conditions.
method: The authors formulate the problem as entropy-regularized exploratory policies, prove equivalence between Nash equilibrium and simultaneous Hamiltonian maximization, and derive a cross-partial criterion for compatibility. They also construct approximate correlated equilibria via coordinate path integrals.
result: Nash equilibria exist unconditionally for decoupled and symmetric games; when compatibility fails, approximate correlated equilibria with explicit KL-divergence bounds are obtained. The framework extends to ergodic settings with locally uniform asymptotic rates.
conclusion: The paper provides a theoretical foundation for multi-agent reinforcement learning in continuous-time stochastic differential games, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimal Placement Of Docking Stations And Resident AUVs For Subsea Pipeline Inspection
authors: Gabriel\.e Kasparavi\v{c}i\=ut\.e, Pasquale Grippa, Kjetil Skaugset, Asgeir J. S{\o}rensen, Martin Ludvigsen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A two-stage mixed-integer linear programming framework is introduced for subsea pipeline incident response planning, jointly optimizing Subsea Docking Plate (SDP) placement and resident autonomous underwater vehicle allocation to minimize both maximum and average response times under spatial uncertainty. Phase 1 minimizes the maximum response time across all potential leak locations. Phase 2 reduces the average response time subject to the maximum bound. A case study based on the Johan Sverdrup oil and gas field in Norway, with 9 SDP options and 33 pipelines, shows that just a few well-placed SDPs are enough to achieve top performance. A cost versus time Pareto analysis reveals the trade-off between deployment expenditure and response efficiency, providing actionable guidance for designing resilient and cost-effective subsea inspection networks.
tldr: This paper optimizes placement of docking stations and AUVs for subsea pipeline inspection using mixed-integer linear programming.
motivation: Subsea pipeline inspection requires efficient response to leaks, but current methods lack joint optimization of docking station placement and AUV allocation.
method: A two-stage MILP framework minimizes maximum response time first, then average response time under that bound, applied to a case study of the Johan Sverdrup field.
result: A few well-placed docking stations achieve near-optimal performance; a Pareto front shows trade-offs between cost and response time.
conclusion: The framework provides actionable guidance for designing cost-effective subsea inspection networks.

title: An Efficient Galerkin Method For High-frequency Scattering Problems Using Wilson Bases
authors: T. Chaumont-Frelet, M. Ingremeau, F. Proust
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a new Galerkin discretization scheme for wave scattering problems that is based on microlocalised basis functions. We show that the proposed method can be made uniformly accurate for large wavenumbers [MATH] with a number of degrees of freedom only scaling as [MATH], while leading to an essentially sparse linear system. In contrast, finite element methods are known to require a number of degrees of freedom scaling at least as [MATH] to achieve the same property. A similar method based on a Gabor frame was previously introduced by two of the authors, but it was suffering from severe conditioning issues. In the present work, by replacing the Gabor frame by a Wilson basis, we completely alleviate this problem. We rigorously establish error estimates and condition number bounds for the proposed method, and we provide one-dimensional numerical examples illustrating our theoretical findings.
tldr: This paper proposes a Galerkin method using Wilson bases for high-frequency wave scattering problems, achieving uniform accuracy with reduced degrees of freedom.
motivation: Standard finite element methods require a large number of degrees of freedom for high-frequency scattering, and previous Gabor frame methods suffered from conditioning issues.
method: The authors replace the Gabor frame with a Wilson basis to construct microlocalised basis functions, and provide error estimates and condition number bounds.
result: The method achieves uniform accuracy for large wavenumbers with degrees of freedom scaling only as O(k^{1/2}), and the linear system is essentially sparse.
conclusion: The Wilson basis approach alleviates conditioning problems and offers an efficient discretization for high-frequency scattering problems.

title: A Third-Order Maximum-Principle-Preserving Cweno Scheme For Two-Dimensional Nonlocal Conservation Laws
authors: Jan Friedrich Anika Beckers
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a third-order finite volume central WENO scheme for systems of nonlocal conservation laws in two spatial dimensions. The CWENO reconstruction of the conservative variable provides polynomials that can be evaluated in the entire domain, which is of advantage when approximating the nonlocal terms. Moreover, this method can be augmented with a limiter that preserves the maximum-principle and especially positivity of the solution.
tldr: This paper presents a third-order finite volume central WENO scheme for two-dimensional nonlocal conservation laws with a maximum-principle-preserving limiter.
motivation: Nonlocal conservation laws arise in various applications, and high-order numerical schemes that preserve the maximum principle are needed for accurate and stable simulations.
method: A third-order CWENO reconstruction is used to obtain polynomials for the conservative variable, which are then integrated with a limiter that ensures the maximum principle and positivity.
result: The proposed scheme achieves third-order accuracy while preserving the maximum principle and positivity for two-dimensional nonlocal conservation laws.
conclusion: The CWENO approach with a limiter is effective for solving nonlocal conservation laws, offering high-order accuracy and essential physical property preservation.

title: Accelerated Stochastic Zeroth-Order Quasar-Convex Optimization
authors: Julien Hermant Em\'eric Gbaguidi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.19965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider unconstrained minimization of smooth quasar-convex functions when only noisy function evaluations are accessible through a stochastic zeroth-order oracle. For these non-convex functions, the standard acceleration method relies on subspace-search mechanisms that require first-order information, being therefore unavailable in zeroth-order regimes. In contrast, the alternative and less conventional continuized method enable to avoid such mechanisms. In this work, we design a zeroth-order continuized algorithm, leading to accelerated convergence guarantees that parallel those of smooth convex optimization up to a quasar-convexity parameter. Our method incorporates a mirror step, improving the dimension dependence when there exists sparse solution.
tldr: This paper proposes an accelerated zeroth-order algorithm for minimizing smooth quasar-convex functions, a class of non-convex functions, using only noisy function evaluations.
motivation: Standard acceleration methods for quasar-convex functions require first-order information, which is unavailable in zeroth-order settings. The authors aim to design an algorithm that achieves accelerated convergence without such information.
method: The authors adapt the continuized method, which avoids subspace-search mechanisms, to the zeroth-order setting. They incorporate a mirror step to improve dimension dependence when the solution is sparse.
result: The proposed algorithm achieves accelerated convergence guarantees that parallel those of smooth convex optimization, up to a quasar-convexity parameter.
conclusion: The work extends accelerated optimization to a broader class of non-convex functions in the zeroth-order regime, with improved dimension dependence for sparse solutions.

title: Order-2 Tightness Of Block-Sparse Sos Relaxations For One-Layer ReLU Network Verification With A Matching Input-Sharing Graph
authors: Godai Azuma, Sunyoung Kim, Makoto Yamashita
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Azuma, Kim, and Yamashita formulated the verification problem for one-layer ReLU networks as a quadratically constrained quadratic program and established tight semidefinite relaxations for the edgeless case and for one-unit settings. In this work, we represent the sharing pattern of undecided ReLUs over a box input set through an input-sharing graph and focus on the case where this graph is a matching. We then derive an explicit, checkable sufficient condition for the tightness of the order-[MATH] block-sparse SOS relaxation associated with the connected-component decomposition of this graph. Under the matching assumption, the global problem decomposes into isolated-vertex blocks and single-edge blocks. The key difficulty, which is absent from the edgeless case, is establishing tightness for a two-unit edge block. For regular rank-one edges, we show that the convex hull of each two-unit local set can be described exactly by two reduced one-unit hulls coupled through a common shared scalar. Combining the one-unit tightness result of Azuma et al. with Farkas' lemma and affine elimination, we obtain a local order-[MATH] certificate for each edge block. Isolated-vertex blocks reduce to one-unit problems over box input sets and are therefore handled at the same order. We prove that, when the input-sharing graph is a matching and every edge satisfies the regular rank-one condition, the order-[MATH] block-sparse SOS relaxation is tight. This extends the tight sparse relaxation result for the edgeless case to the first sparse setting with a nontrivial two-unit interaction.
